system.name: Tintin
system.one_liner: a unified hardware-performance-profiling infrastructure that quantifies uncertainty in performance counters and uses it for scheduling

components.name: Applications
components.role: user-space programs whose requests trigger profiling via the API

components.role: interface applications use to issue profiling requests to the Manager

components.name: Manager
components.role: exposes the API, holds contexts and events/profiling-scope configuration, and returns HPC data with uncertainty to applications

components.name: Events of interest
components.role: configuration of which hardware events to profile

components.name: Profiling scopes
components.role: configuration of the code/time scope to profile

components.name: Scheduler
components.role: sets a scheduling policy meant to minimize measurement uncertainty, using the uncertainty delta reported by the Monitor

components.name: Monitor
components.role: tracks event counts and characterizes their uncertainty at runtime from the microarchitectural event source

components.role: hardware performance-counter source read by the Monitor

flows.what: event counts and profiling scopes to track

content.key_idea: Tintin factors hardware-performance profiling into three kernel components: a Manager that exposes contexts/events/scopes to applications, a Monitor that tracks event counts and their uncertainty from microarchitectural sources, and a Scheduler that uses that uncertainty to pick scheduling policies that minimize it.
content.reading_order: Top-down: Applications issuing a request across the User/Kernel boundary into the Manager, then down into the Scheduler and Monitor exchanging uncertainty and scheduling decisions.

Tintin-Monitor (§5) measures HPC data and characterizes errors simultaneously at runtime

summary: This figure gives Tintin's design overview: a hardware-performance-profiling infrastructure split into three kernel-resident modules below a User/Kernel boundary. Applications issue a request across that boundary to the Manager, which holds per-request Contexts plus configured Events of interest and Profiling scopes, and returns HPC data together with its uncertainty. Internally, the Manager hands scheduling policy to the Scheduler and event/profiling configuration to the Monitor. The Monitor reads raw counts from a uArch Event Source, tracks event counts, and computes an uncertainty value; it reports an Uncertainty Delta to the Scheduler, which returns a scheduling decision aimed at minimizing that uncertainty. A dashed cloud beside Applications lists example uses - anomaly detection, resource orchestration, energy analysis, workload optimization, debugging - motivating why applications would consume uncertainty-aware profiling data.

notes: Body paragraph is truncated right after naming Tintin-Monitor, so the Manager and Scheduler roles are read from the figure's own labels rather than confirmed by text. layout-proposal: two-tier boundary with an interacting module triangle — a User/Kernel horizontal split contains three peer modules (Manager, Scheduler, Monitor) exchanging data bidirectionally rather than stacking as sequential layers.
